sections.label: Girl's education cut short
sections.summary: As eldest daughter, her schooling was stopped after two years because her parents thought girls needed little education.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As the eldest child and being a daughter, her childhood was often a battle between herself and her parents who felt that it was unseemly for girls to not only be seen running around outdoors but for them to be educated.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: She was allowed to start Primary school but was pulled out two years later when it was deemed this was more than enough education a girl would need.

sections.label: Popo's regret and granddaughters
sections.summary: Popo regretted being born a girl and denied further education, but her nine granddaughters led very different lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I know that it was a bitter regret of Popo's that she was born a girl and that she was not allowed to further her education as a result.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But by the time she passed away five years ago, aged 99, her nine granddaughters have led hugely different lives from being the first Singaporean woman on Everest, authoring best-selling cookbooks, studying, living and working on five continents and speaking here today in this House.

sections.label: 2021 Year to SG Celebrate Women
sections.summary: After last year's General Election, the Government announced 2021 as the Year to SG Celebrate Women.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just after the General Election last year, the Government announced that 2021 would be designated as the Year to SG Celebrate Women.

sections.label: Singapore's Gender Inequality Index rank
sections.summary: The UN Development Report 2020 ranked Singapore 12th worldwide for the Gender Inequality Index.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The UN Development Report in 2020 ranked Singapore 12th in the world for the Gender Inequality Index, behind countries such as Switzerland, Denmark and South Korea.

sections.label: Women's caring burden and gender equality
sections.summary: Women fill caring professions and mothers bore home burdens, so these issues must be addressed post-pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Again, the answer is that across all societies, women make up the bulk of those in the caring professions such as nursing and social care, who have been stretched to their limits in the last 18 months, and at home it is often mothers who have taken on the burden as we juggled home-based work, home-schooling, childcare and housework.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is only right that we address these issues now, as we emerge into a post-pandemic world, to ensure that we do not fall behind in the progress made thus far.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And for those who feel that gender equality is a largely philosophical exercise, perhaps speak to a woman who is denied a pay increment or job offer because of her gender or status as a mother.

sections.label: Women's work seen as inferior
sections.summary: Work traditionally done by women is still viewed as inferior or ancillary to wage-earning work.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Work traditionally done by women such as caring, running households and looking after our families, continue to be seen as being inferior or merely ancillary to the "real work" of earning wages.

sections.label: Media questions on single women
sections.summary: A CNA article on highly educated single women asked whether they are too picky, busy, independent or intimidating, questions the speaker doubts would be asked of men.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, in a CNA article dated 30 June 2021, which attempted to explore the trend of highly educated women remaining single, the questions asked were, I quote, "are they too picky, too busy, too independent, too intimidating?" I am just not sure if we will ever see questions like these being asked if a highly educated unmarried man in his 40s were to be presented as the same.

sections.label: Tax reliefs for re-entry programmes
sections.summary: The 2020 manifesto proposed tax reliefs for employers running successful re-entry programmes for mothers and informal carers who took time off for caring responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our 2020 manifesto's specific proposal was for tax reliefs to be granted to employers to run successful re-entry programmes for mothers and informal carers who have taken time off to fulfil their caring responsibilities.

sections.label: TAFEP regime accountability gaps
sections.summary: The current TAFEP regime does not go far enough in providing accountability for perpetrators and places the reporting burden on the victim.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The current TAFEP regime does not go far enough in providing a framework for accountability for perpetrators and neglects the nuances of such situations by placing the burden of reporting the incident on the victim.

sections.label: Egg and sperm preservation centre
sections.summary: The centre should offer egg and sperm preservation for married couples, and laws banning egg freezing for non-medical reasons should be re-examined with accessibility in mind.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This centre should also look to offering preservation of eggs and sperm to benefit married couples for whom this option may be necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There should also be a wider conversation about re-looking the laws that currently ban egg freezing for non-medical reasons, with any proposed amendments or solutions bearing in mind not only the concerns raised by some of us, but also whether such procedures will be accessible to different socio-economic groups.

sections.label: Ipsos study on mothers' strain
sections.summary: A May Ipsos study in Singapore found household and care responsibilities strained more than half of mothers, with similar numbers lacking time for their well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, a study by Ipsos in May this year here in Singapore found that household and care responsibilities were sources of strain for more than half of mothers, with similar figures reporting not having the time to look after their physical, mental and emotional well-being.

sections.label: UN Women unpaid work estimate
sections.summary: UN Women estimated women did three times as much unpaid work as men before the pandemic, and the figure has at least doubled since.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In fact, UN Women has estimated that while women were doing three times as much unpaid work as men before the pandemic, the figure has at least doubled since the pandemic hit.

sections.label: COVID-19 impact on women
sections.summary: AWARE reported a 137% rise in family violence calls during lockdown, and the speaker calls for government data and longitudinal studies on COVID-19's impact on women.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE) reported increases of 137% in the number of family violence calls during our lockdown last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What is equally alarming is that there appears to be a limited number of Singapore-specific studies available, which leaves us in the dark as to the true impact of COVID-19 on women here.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, believe that the Government has to study and publish its data and statistics to measure the adverse impact COVID-19 has had on women, and also to carry out longitudinal studies to measure the different spheres in which women have been adversely affected, and to catch any trends before these reversals become hard-baked into our economy and society.

sections.label: Women and Basic Retirement Sum
sections.summary: In 2018, only 56% of women met the Basic Retirement Sum in their CPF accounts compared to 67% of men.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, it was found that women have more difficulty than men when it comes to meeting the Basic Retirement Sum in their CPF accounts, with only 56% of women meeting the amount compared to 67% for men in 2018.

sections.label: CareShield Life gender premiums
sections.summary: The speaker says Sylvia Lim and Pritam Singh noted CareShield Life's impact on women's labour force participation and that gender-based treatment contradicts universality and risk-pooling.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2018, when CareShield Life was introduced, my colleague Sylvia Lim and Pritam Singh, the Members for Aljunied GRC, pointed out not only the devastating impact this would have on women's participation in the labour force, but also fundamentally how this difference in treatment along gender lines directly contradicts the scheme's intended features of "universality" and "risk-pooling".

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Apart from being unfair to women, this sets a dangerous precedent where we differentiate policy application within society.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, if life expectancy differs between races and socio-economic groups, would different premiums then be justifiable between these groups, depending on how we splice the population?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: National policies such as CareShield Life should pool risk across differences and instead share the burden of care, especially as our population ages.

sections.label: Older women's CPF balances
sections.summary: Older women have 12% to 25% less in CPF than older men, and 15,000 persons topped up spouses' CPF in 2020, up from 11,000 in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Older women have 12% to 25% less in their CPF compared to older men, depending on the age bracket.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government currently encourages husbands to voluntarily transfer funds to their wife’s CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifteen thousand persons topped up their spouses’ CPF in 2020, up from 11,000 in 2018.

sections.label: Homemaker contribution research
sections.summary: The speaker suggests researching the commercial value of a homemaker's contribution to assess whether to raise matching or tax reliefs for husbands' CPF transfers to wives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As a start, I would suggest that research be undertaken on the commercial value of a homemaker’s contribution and that this be used as a reference point in determining if there is a need to raise the Government quantum or ceiling for dollar-for-dollar matching of husband’s CPF transfers to their wives or the tax reliefs to the husbands for the same; or other policy interventions.

sections.label: Discrimination cases and perceptions
sections.summary: TAFEP handled about 400 discrimination cases yearly, a third gender or age related, and perceived job-search discrimination rose from 10% in 2014 to 15% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the answer to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I filed in March this year, TAFEP handled an average of around 400 discrimination cases each year for the past three years, about a third of which related to gender or age discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In about 50 cases each year, or 13% of cases, the employers were found to be in breach of the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices and had their foreign work pass privileges suspended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From the reply to a PQ I filed in February last year and a report released in November, the percentage of Singaporeans who perceived discrimination during their job search process has increased from 10% in 2014 to 15% in 2018.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination laws clarity
sections.summary: The Workers' Party says anti-discrimination laws give clarity on offences and clear investigative and prosecutorial responsibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The advantage of anti-discrimination laws, which the Workers’ Party called for in its 2020 GE manifesto, is that there is necessarily clarity on what constitutes an offence; and a clear line of investigative and prosecutorial responsibility for enforcing the law against offenders.

sections.label: Teaching gender equality in schools
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to ensure Secondary school students are taught the principles of gender equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In an Adjournment Motion, my colleague Ms Raeesah Khan spoke about the need for the education system to teach the notion of consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would urge the Government to also ensure that Secondary school students are taught the principles of gender equality, as Ms He Ting Ru referred to: what it is, why it is important and what laws and provisions buttress this principle in Singapore.

sections.label: Female instructors for NSFs
sections.summary: Efforts should be made to ensure most batches of NSFs train under at least one or a few female instructors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Efforts should also be made to ensure that most batches of NSFs train under at least one or a few female instructors.

sections.label: Workers' Party stands for workers
sections.summary: The Workers' Party will always stand up for workers facing unequal treatment, whether male or female.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party will always stand up for workers that are facing problems with unequal treatment, whether male or female.

sections.label: Existing gender inequalities listed
sections.summary: The passage states that sexist discrimination, harassment, COVID-19 effects, wage gaps, CareShield Life premiums and housework burdens still exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Sexist discrimination at work still exists; sexual harassment and assault against women by men still exists, the unequal effect of COVID-19 on women exists, a gender wage gap and unequal CareShield Life premiums still exist, working women bearing an unequal burden of housework and parenting and losing out in their career still happens, along with many other aspects of the gender equality problem that we shall touch on.

sections.label: Measuring gender equality success
sections.summary: The passage says success in gender equality means society stops boxing women into stereotypes, and notes 160 Conversations held since September 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a good way to measure the success of any policy we adopt, and that should be continued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I would like to add that in the case of gender equality, the biggest indicator of success will be when we, as a society, stop boxing women into long-held stereotypes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead of the term "girl boss", why not just "boss"?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Instead of struggling between being a stay-at-home mom and giving up one's career, on the one hand, or being a working mum and facing certain disadvantages and losing out while facing "mom guilt", is it too much of an ideal to expect that one day, women will, by and large, have the tools and means to combine both roles comfortably?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Achieving that balance will go far in benefiting not just women, but the progress of Singapore as a whole.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since the Government launched the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development in September 2020, we have held 160 conversations involving more than 5,700 participants from all walks of life.

sections.label: 1957 women literacy and employment
sections.summary: In 1957, women's general literacy rate was 29% and 21.6% of women aged 15 and above were economically active.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the census of 1957, the general literacy rate of women in Singapore was 29% and only 21.6% of the total female population aged 15 years and above were economically active.

sections.label: Women's Charter Bill 1960
sections.summary: Minister KM Bryne presented the Women's Charter Bill in 1960, leading to the 1961 Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Minister for Labour and Law Mr KM Bryne presented the Women's Charter Bill to the First Session of the First Legislative Assembly of the State of Singapore on 2 March 1960.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: At the Second Reading of the Bill, he said, "The Government is carrying out its promise... that it will enact legislation which... will make it an offence to contract other than monogamous marriages... and to consolidate the existing laws relating to marriage, divorce, the rights and duties of married persons, the maintenance of wives and children, and the punishment of offences against women and girls." This paved the way for the passage of the Women's Charter in 1961, which was significant, as it raised the social standing of women by institutionalising the equal standing of men and women in marriage and ensuring the welfare and protection of women in Singapore.

sections.label: Female literacy rate rise
sections.summary: Female literacy rose from 29% in 1957 to 54.3% in 1970 and crossed 80% in 1988.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Female literacy rate went from 29% in 1957, to 54.3% in 1970 and crossed 80% in 1988.

sections.label: Female labour force participation
sections.summary: Female labour force participation for ages 25 to 64 was 51.5% in 1991 and is 76.6% now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 1991, the female labour force participation rate for those aged 25 to 64 was 51.5%, and stands at 76.6% now.

sections.label: Conversations on Singapore Women's Development
sections.summary: Sixty years after the Bill, the Government launched Conversations on Singapore Women's Development, hearing from over 5,700 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Exactly 60 years later from the passing of the Women's Charter Bill, the Government of Singapore launched the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development to chart the next lap forward for our women's progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: There was an open call to the public to participate in the Conversations and we heard from more than 5,700 participants.

sections.label: Penalties for sexual offences
sections.summary: MHA reviewed sentencing for sexual and hurt offences and increased penalties for three specific sexual offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To enhance protection for women, MHA has reviewed the sentencing framework for sexual and hurt offences and increased the penalties for three specific sexual offences.

sections.label: Prime Minister Conversations final session
sections.summary: The Prime Minister will attend the final Conversations session in September and share future plans based on feedback received.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Given the importance of Singapore women's progress to our nation, the Prime Minister will be attending the final session of the Conversations in September and he will be sharing our plans for the future, taking into consideration the feedback received from the Conversations.

sections.label: Matched Retirement Savings and Silver Support
sections.summary: The Government introduced the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme and increased Silver Support Scheme subsidies in recent years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In recent years, the Government has introduced the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to increase their CPF savings and also, increased subsidies through the Silver Support Scheme.

sections.label: 160 Conversations on Women's Development
sections.summary: Over 10 months, 160 Conversations on Singapore Women's Development were held with community partners and 5,700 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Over the past 10 months, together with community partners, we have organised 160 Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development, with a total of 5,700 participants.

sections.label: White Paper to Parliament
sections.summary: After the conversations, feedback will be consolidated and a White Paper drawn up to submit to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: After the series of conversations, we will consolidate the feedback and draw up a White Paper to submit to Parliament.

sections.label: Study on household and caregiving
sections.summary: A study found most agree chores can be shared equally, but fewer women than men are happy with household and caring responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on a study by market research firm Ipos and United Women Singapore (UWS), close to nine in 10 agree that household chores can be equally shared by husband and wife.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, fewer women, or about 54%, than men, or about 75%, say that they are happy about their household and caring responsibilities, with wider gap between mothers and fathers at 47% and 78% respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on MOM's Labour Force in Singapore 2020 report, women represented 63% of residents outside the labour force as of June 2020 or 689,400 out of the total of 1.1 million residents.

sections.label: Men and women caregiving responsibilities
sections.summary: Fewer men than women were outside the labour force for care responsibilities, echoing an MSF survey on caregiving attitudes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, only 2.5% of men were outside the labour force due to care responsibilities for their own children and family members, which is, again, significantly different from that of women at 15.9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This echoes an MSF survey on social attitudes of Singaporeans, where 96% of married working women indicated that they were equally or primarily responsible for caregiving responsibilities, compared to 53% of married working men.

sections.label: Ageing society and moral duty
sections.summary: An ageing society creates a moral duty to care for parents, with 183,000 young children versus 611,000 elderly as of June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With an increasingly ageing society, we also have a moral duty to take care of our parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And as of June 2020, the population of children between age zero and four is at 183,000 as compared to 611,000 elderly citizens aged 65 and above, with our population continuing to age.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements legislation
sections.summary: In 2019 about 85% of employers offered flexible work arrangements, and the Government should legislate a baseline level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2019, it was said that about 85% of employers offered some form of formal or ad hoc FWAs in the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As I have shared in my MOM COS speech, it is now time for the Government to reflect the needs of today's employees and employers, and legislate a baseline level of flexible work arrangement, so that we do not have to make the false choice of choosing between work or family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even if eldercare leave is available, it is currently not a legislative requirement, some in Singapore may not be eligible for it if they are caring for a spouse and are elderly themselves.

sections.label: Workers' Party shared parental leave
sections.summary: The Workers' Party manifesto calls for 24 weeks of shared Government-paid parental leave, replacing 16-week maternity and two-week paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party has in our manifesto called for a shared parental leave scheme that entitles parents to 24 weeks of Government-paid leave, to be shared between mothers and fathers as they choose, but with a minimum of 12 weeks to be granted to the mother and four weeks to the father.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This scheme would replace the existing 16-week maternity and two-week paternity leave entitlements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, we are looking at 24 weeks instead of 18 weeks in total, of gender-neutral parental leave.

sections.label: Childcare places in Sengkang
sections.summary: Increased infant and childcare places remain inadequate in towns like Sengkang, which has 16,380 zero- to four-year-olds as of June 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my MSF COS speech earlier this year, I noted that while the Government has increased the number of infant care and childcare places over the last five years, this is still woefully inadequate in towns such as Sengkang, which has the highest number of young children across Singapore by planning area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There are 16,380 zero- to four-year-olds and 17,600 five- to nine-year-olds as of June 2020.

sections.label: Women's Charter 1961
sections.summary: The 1961 Women's Charter focused on legal equality for women, making polygamy an offence and setting a minimum marriage age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore had a jump start in women's rights with the Women's Charter in 1961, which was focused on legal equality for women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This included making polygamy an offence, prohibiting marriages between close relations and including a minimum age for marriage.

sections.label: Conversations on Women Development
sections.summary: The Government conducted a series of dialogues called Conversations on Women Development, with 160 such talks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last year, for example, the Government started conducting a series of dialogues called "Conversations on Women Development".

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As Ms Sun Xueling mentioned earlier, there were 160 such talks.

sections.label: Older women caregivers job challenges
sections.summary: Older women who left work for caregiving struggle to find jobs again, though childcare and senior care facilities help; senior care support lags behind childcare support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Older women who have taken several years to be out of the workforce for caregiving duties, have challenges finding jobs again, even though they may have relevant skills and qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to caregiving, some mentioned that the availability of childcare and senior care facilities have been helpful in allowing them to minimise time out of the workforce in order to care for loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, they also mentioned that support for those caring for seniors is still lagging behind the extensive support that there is already for childcare.

sections.label: Stigma against unconventional living situations
sections.summary: Stigma was raised against women in unconventional living situations, including single unwed mothers who cannot get many benefits married mothers receive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In addition, another topic that was raised was the stigma women faced when in unconventional living situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These include single unwed mothers who are unable to get many of the benefits that married mothers could, even though they are usually in a worse-off situation.

sections.label: White Paper on women's development
sections.summary: The Government announced in September last year it would present a White Paper from its Conversations on Singapore Women's Development findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to this, the Government had announced in September last year that it would be presenting a White Paper arising from its findings from the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development.

sections.label: Proposed words tie Motion to action
sections.summary: The additional words proposed tie the spirit of the Motion to concrete action, which the Member hopes the Government will put forward in its White Paper.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The additional words I am proposing are to tie the spirit of the Motion with concrete action, which I hope the Government will put forward in its White Paper.

sections.label: Amendment and simultaneous debate proposal
sections.summary: An amendment adds words after "society" looking forward to action plans in the upcoming White Paper, and debate on the Motion and amendments may proceed simultaneously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: I am sure they too would want to see what plans the Government has in store as well for these issues being raised.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: It has been proposed as an amendment, in line 3 after the word "society", to add the following words: "and looks forward to action plans in the upcoming Government White Paper arising out of the Conversations on Singapore Women's Development".

sentences.speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: It may be convenient that the debate on the original Motion and on any other amendments moved by Members be proceeded with simultaneously as a debate on a single Question.

sections.label: Four areas and sexual violence cases
sections.summary: The Member focuses on sexual violence, female genital cutting, polygamy and the hijab, sharing that underaged cases were 37% of sexual violence cases in 2017 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I want to focus on four main areas: sexual violence, female genital cutting, polygamy and the hijab.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I shared that underaged cases made up 37% of sexual violence cases between 2017 and 2019.

sections.label: US sex crimes study
sections.summary: A US study found persons with intellectual disabilities were sexually assaulted at rates over seven times higher than others.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the US, a study on sex crimes data found that persons with intellectual disabilities of all genders were victims of sexual assault at rates over seven times higher than those of persons without intellectual disabilities.

sections.label: Survivor support services question
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for Social and Family Development about Ministry and agency work on longer-term survivor support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister for Social and Family Development share on current work done by the Ministry and other Government agencies to offer robust and accessible survivor support in the medium to longer term, including but not limited to psychologists, therapists and support group linkages?

sections.label: Female genital cutting in Singapore
sections.summary: The passage defines female genital cutting and states the practice, known as Sunat Perempuan, continues in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I move on to the topic of female genital cutting or FGC, defined by UNICEF as the injury, partial, or total removal of the external female genital organs for non-medical reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This practice – Sunat Perempuan, as it is known in Malay – continues in Singapore, quiet though it may be.

sections.label: Review of FGC procedures
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to review female genital cutting in private clinics, standardise skin cut, ensure instrumentation and require counselling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Noting the pain that such acts can bring to females undergoing such practices, I strongly urge the MOH to conduct a thorough review of female genital cutting procedures done in private clinics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We should aim to standardise and make transparent the amount of skin cut during the procedure, or enforce that the practice should be purely symbolic, ensure that the proper instrumentation is used, and, as with similar types of medical procedures, require medical counselling for those who seek to carry it out.

sections.label: Mandatory 48-hour counselling period
sections.summary: After counselling, a mandatory 48-hour period is proposed before parents may arrange another appointment to proceed with cutting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: After counselling, there should be a mandatory 48-hour period, after which, if the parents still wish to proceed with the cutting, they may arrange another appointment.

sections.label: First steps on polygamy
sections.summary: The passage suggests making the existing wife's consent mandatory for second marriages, as done in Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But if banning polygamy outright is too much for now, perhaps we can begin with some first steps.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We can make the consent of the existing wife mandatory for second marriages, as is done in Indonesia.

sections.label: Marriage contract no second wife
sections.summary: An option is to add a clause in the marriage certificate stipulating a husband cannot take another wife.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Another option is to include an additional clause in the "automatic" standard and printed clauses in the marriage certificate, stipulating in the marriage contract that a husband cannot take another wife.

sections.label: Nurse faith and family
sections.summary: A nurse told the speaker she felt torn between her faith and providing for her family, and the Government will review nurses donning the hijab.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, one resident, a nurse, approached me sharing that she felt torn that she had to choose between her faith and providing for her family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am glad to hear that the Government will be reviewing their position on nurses donning the hijab.

sections.label: Hijabs in UK and US
sections.summary: Royal Derby Hospital staff receive disposable sterile headscarves, and the US army made hijabs part of its uniform in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the Royal Derby Hospital in the UK, staff receive disposable sterile headscarves, and the US army has made hijabs part of its uniform in 2017.

sections.label: Tangs employee hijab removal
sections.summary: A Tangs employee was asked to remove her hijab to be hired as a promoter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, we have evidence of this happening, such as the Tangs employee who was asked to remove her hijab to be hired as a promoter.

sections.label: Dual-income couples census increase
sections.summary: The Population Census showed dual-income couples increased from 52.9% in 2010 to 60% last year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Population Census showed that dual-income couples have increased from 52.9% in 2010, to 60% last year.

sections.label: Surveys on caregiving gender
sections.summary: A 2012 MCYS survey found about 60% female and 40% male caregivers, and more unemployed female residents cited caregiving as the main reason for leaving jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2012, the then MCYS commissioned a survey on informal caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They found more female caregivers, about 60%, as compared to male caregivers, about 40%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More recently, the MOM Report on Labour force in Singapore 2020 saw that for unemployed residents who cited caregiving as the main reason for leaving their jobs, more than two times of them are female.

sections.label: Women's jobs more vulnerable
sections.summary: McKinsey states women's jobs are 1.8 times more vulnerable in this crisis than men's jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to McKinsey, women's jobs are 1.8 times more vulnerable in this crisis than men's jobs.

sections.label: Re-educating society on shared responsibilities
sections.summary: A whole-of-society mindset shift is needed to re-educate society on shared responsibilities in the home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   We need a whole-of-society and community mindset shift to re-educate the society on shared responsibilities in the home.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our boys will grow up to be colleagues, husbands and fathers, and we will raise them to treat women with dignity, honour and respect.

sections.label: Solidarity with marginalised women
sections.summary: We should act in solidarity with women from marginalised groups: the old, differently-abled, poor or single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To raise each other up, we should also act in solidarity with the women from marginalised groups: the old, the differently-abled, the poor or the single mother trying her best to raise strong confident daughters of her own.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To raise each other up, we should also act in solidarity with the women from marginalised groups: the old, the differently-abled, the poor, or the single mother trying her best to raise strong confident daughters of her own.

sections.label: Sister Annabella Sim founding chairperson
sections.summary: Sister Annabella Sim, then 21, became founding chairperson of the NTUC Women's Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Sister Annabella Sim, then just 21, a visionary whose form many of us take after today, became the founding chairperson of the NTUC Women's Committee and, I would say, the first female elected to our Central Committee.

sections.label: Yu-Foo Yee Shoon expanded childcare centres
sections.summary: Mrs Yu-Foo Yee Shoon and the unions took over and expanded the Department of Social Welfare's 10 childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On being willing to put in the hard work: in response to women's waning labour force participation rates after childbirth years, Mrs Yu-Foo Yee Shoon and the unions took over and expanded the then Department of Social Welfare's 10 childcare centres.

sections.label: NTUC First Campus childcare today
sections.summary: The seed Mrs Yu-Foo sowed is now NTUC First Campus, providing affordable childcare through 160 preschool centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The seed Mrs Yu-Foo had sown almost 50 years ago is what is known today as NTUC First Campus, which continues to provide affordable childcare through its 160 preschool centres island-wide and nine Primary-school-based student care centres serving more than 20,000 families.

sections.label: Childcare subsidies and centres
sections.summary: Childcare subsidies were enhanced in 2020 and full-day childcare and infant care centre places rose from 140,000 to 190,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Childcare subsidies were further enhanced in 2020 and the number of full-day childcare and infant care centres has risen from 140,000 to 190,000.

sections.label: Back2Work and workplace harassment
sections.summary: Back2Work helped over 28,000 women return to work and trained over 30,000, and tripartite workplace harassment measures were drawn up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Over the years, the Back2Work Programme has helped more than 28,000 women return to work and provided training to more than 30,000 women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Companies such as Le Essen, a catering and canteen operator, now have 50% of their workforce comprising women returning to work on redesigned flexible work hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Indeed, in the area of workplace harassment, the tripartite partners have also drawn up a tripartite advisory on managing workplace harassment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: NTUC has also developed a workplace harassment prevention policy to be adopted and adapted by companies and, indeed, both are promoted by TAFEP.

sections.label: Foreign spouses' visit pass applications
sections.summary: From February to July 2020, ICA received 8,395 applications for extensions of Short-Term Visit Passes from foreign spouses of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to an answer to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I asked last September, in the six months from February to July 2020, the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) received 8,395 applications for extensions of Short-Term Visit Passes (STVPs) from foreign spouses of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Rejected visit pass applications
sections.summary: Over 250 applications were rejected during the six-month period last year, though the vast majority were approved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the vast majority of applications are approved, over 250 were rejected during the six-month period last year.

sections.label: Single mothers' income and housing
sections.summary: Single unmarried mothers below 35 had a median monthly income of $600 in 2017, and many single parents cannot buy or rent subsidised HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to a reply to a PQ by Mr Louis Ng, the median monthly income from work of single, unmarried mothers below the age of 35 was just $600 in 2017, which was 86% less than the national median income that year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, many single parents are not eligible to buy or rent a subsidised HDB flat to live with their children.

sections.label: Singles and single parents housing
sections.summary: Singles below 35 cannot buy HDB flats or rent under the Public Rental Scheme, and single parents should be allowed PPHS rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singles below the age of 35 do not qualify to purchase HDB flats or rent flats under the Public Rental Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Single parents awaiting the construction of their BTO flats should also be allowed to rent a flat under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS), which is currently available only to married couples, divorcees or the widowed.

sections.label: Man applying for ex-wife maintenance
sections.summary: A man with custody of the children and much lower earning power than his ex-wife should be allowed to apply for maintenance from her.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A man should be allowed to apply for maintenance from his ex-wife if he has custody of their children and has a much lower earning power than her.

sections.label: Women's labour force participation gap
sections.summary: The labour force participation rate of women trails men by 14%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The labour force participation rate of women trails 14% behind men.

sections.label: Questions on Police case handling
sections.summary: Any questions about how the Police handled or mishandled this case should be investigated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Any form of questions raised about how the Police have handled or mishandled this case should be investigated.

sections.label: Police mishandling allegation and Parliamentary Questions
sections.summary: Reports to Police and other institutions matter, information requests should be filed as Parliamentary Questions, and the serious allegation of Police mishandling will be looked into.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan
sentences.text: This may not just be when they make reports to the Police but it can also be how they make reports to other institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I had requested that if you have specific questions or requests for information, you should file a proper Parliamentary Question so that we can provide the data to you properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: I would also like to say that you have made a very serious allegation of the mishandling by Police in the House through your speech and we take this seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
sentences.text: We would like to have the details so that we can look into it and not just have this swept aside.

sections.label: Suggestions and policy changes for women
sections.summary: Since entering the House in 2011, the speaker has heard many suggestions from Members of Parliament and seen policy changes implemented to support Singapore women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Since I entered this House in 2011, I have heard many suggestions made by fellow Members of Parliament and have also seen real policy changes being implemented to resolve pain points and provide stronger support to Singapore women.

sections.label: 2017 Private Members' Motion on women
sections.summary: In 2017, the speaker and fellow PAP women Members of Parliament moved a Private Members' Motion titled "Aspirations of Women".

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: More recently, in 2017, I, together with fellow PAP women Members of Parliament – Mdm Deputy Speaker Jessica Tan, Miss Cheryl Chan, Ms Joan Pereira and former Member of Parliament Er Dr Lee Bee Wah – moved a Private Members' Motion titled "Aspirations of Women".

sections.label: Support for women caregivers
sections.summary: The debate covered four strategies to support Singapore women, noting women still take the primary caregiving role, so more caregiver support and care options were sought.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Through the two-day debate, colleagues and I articulated and elaborated on the four strategies that we believed were critical to supporting Singapore women in their aspirational pursuits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We agreed that, as of the current reality, the primary caregiving role was still undertaken by women and, therefore, we called for more support to our caregivers, including enhancing availability and access to care options so as to free up women's capacity to pursue their aspirations, career- or social-wise.

sections.label: PAP Women's Wing recommendation
sections.summary: The recommendation was also pushed by the PAP Women's Wing in 2015 as "Top Up with Love", and the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme was implemented this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I should add that this recommendation was also something that the PAP Women's Wing pushed for in 2015 and we called it "Top Up with Love".

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Also, from this year, the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme was also implemented.

sections.label: Increase in care places
sections.summary: Home care and day care places rose to 10,300 and 9,000 in 2019, while infant care and childcare centres increased from 2017 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For instance, the number of home care and day care places increased to 10,300 and 9,000 respectively in 2019, exceeding the 2020 targets announced in 2017 back then.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Infant care centres increased from 512 in 2017 to 661 in 2020, and childcare centres increased from 1,389 in 2017 to 1,542 in 2020.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements adoption
sections.summary: About 85% of employers offered flexible work arrangements in 2019, and over 8,000 companies adopted the Tripartite Standard on FWAs by end-November 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In 2019, about 85% of employers offered some form of FWAs and this number increased during the COVID-19 period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As of end-November 2020, more than 8,000 companies adopted the Tripartite Standard on FWAs, up from under 2,000 companies a year ago.

sections.label: PAP women's development recommendations
sections.summary: The PAP submitted 12 recommendations to the Government last week to promote women's development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In response, the PAP submitted 12 recommendations to the Government last week to promote women’s development.

sections.label: White Paper on women
sections.summary: The Government is tabling a White Paper this year, with PAP, AWARE and WP submitting recommendations, and the House is asked to affirm Singapore women's contributions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, our endeavour to support Singapore women must continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And I believe that it is in this spirit that the Government is tabling a White Paper later this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Contributing to this White Paper, the PAP submitted our recommendations to the Government last week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Likewise, AWARE and WP have put forth theirs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But even as we continue to co-create these solutions, I believe it is important that this House affirms the familial, social and economic contributions of Singapore women and our support for them to fulfil their aspirations and societal participation, and we look forward to the White Paper.

sections.label: Singapore women in parliament ranking
sections.summary: Singapore, with nearly 30% female Members of Parliament, is ranked 54th, behind Nordic countries, Rwanda and the UAE.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore, with its nearly 30% female Members of Parliament, is ranked 54th in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore lags significantly behind the Nordic countries as well as Rwanda and the UAE which have between 40% and 61% of women legislators.

sections.label: Government advocating women directors
sections.summary: The Singapore Government has been advocating that company boards should aim for 30% women directors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government has been advocating that boards of companies should aim to have 30% of women directors.

sections.label: Women subjugated by male party leaders
sections.summary: Some women seeking priority on lists faced whimsical decisions and humiliating demands from male party leaders, and legal quotas should be avoided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, in some instances, women who wished to be prioritised on the list were subjugated to the whimsical decision-making of their male party leaders, including acceding to humiliating demands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should not go down this route of legal quotas.

sections.label: Women candidates in last General Election
sections.summary: In the last General Election, nearly 27% of ruling party candidates and nearly 24% of Workers' Party candidates were women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we look at the last General Election, on the ruling party side, nearly 27% of the candidates were women, while on the Workers’ Party side, nearly 24% were women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After Polling Day, female PAP Members of Parliament formed about 29% of PAP Members of Parliament, while female WP Members of Parliament formed 30% of WP Members of Parliament.

sections.label: Female Ministers in Cabinet
sections.summary: The Cabinet has three female Ministers out of 20, which is 15%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When it comes to the Cabinet, we see three female Ministers out of 20, which is 15%.

sections.label: Singapore gender gap ranking
sections.summary: Singapore was 54th globally in the gender gap assessment, the same ranking as its female parliamentary representation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to this gender gap assessment, Singapore was 54th globally, coincidentally the same ranking we received on the percentage of female representation in Parliament.

sections.label: Buy-in for women's aspirations
sections.summary: Government, employers, employees, business and family must buy in so wives, mothers and daughters can fulfil aspirations and contribute to public life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Government, employers, employees, business and family must buy-in to this vision, in order that our wives, mothers and daughters can fulfil their aspirations and contribute to public life if they wish to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of the moments that moved me greatly was the victory ceremony for a relatively new event in swimming – the four by 100m mixed medley relay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was so refreshing to see the teams of four swimmers at the victory podium – two men and two women – showing the world the glory that their combined effort had brought to their countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Each of them, man, and woman, was equally critical in achieving the team's success.

sections.label: Female labour force participation rise
sections.summary: Female labour force participation rose from around 45% in 1990 to around 62% in 2019, the latest available data.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Between 1990 and 2019, for example, the female labour force participation rate has risen from around 45% in 1990, to around 62% in 2019, the latest year that data are available and, unfortunately, a number that differs from Minister of State Sun Xueling's earlier citation, unless I misheard, of 76%.

sections.label: Male participation rate outstrips women
sections.summary: Over the same period the male participation rate continued to outstrip women's, ranging between 78% and 79% over three decades.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Over the same period, the male participation rate continued to outstrip that of women, ranging between 78% and 79% over the past three decades.

sections.label: Married employment and part-time figures
sections.summary: In 2017, 83.4% of married men were employed versus 63.3% of married women, and women were 64% of part-time participation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The numbers corroborate this story: in Singapore, 83.4% of married men were employed in 2017, while in contrast, only 63.3% of married women stayed in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For that same year, women accounted for 64% of part-time labour force participation, almost twice as many as men, who accounted for the remaining 36%.

sections.label: Income differential and career discount
sections.summary: Singapore's income differential is around 16.3%, implying over a 40-year median-salary career a discount of a little more than a third of $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In Singapore, this income differential is around average compared to other industrialised economies, at 16.3%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To put this number in context though, this gap implies that, to a worker earning the median salary over a 40-year career, this discount experienced by women amounts to around a little more than a third of $1 million.

sections.label: Halving the gap
sections.summary: Doing so turns out to half the gap to around 6%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Doing so turns out to half the gap to around 6%.

sections.label: Removing hurdles for women leaders
sections.summary: It proposes removing barriers to women's leadership training and considering reserved board seats for women in GLCs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hurdles for women to participate in high-performance leadership training – such as how heavy travel commitments preclude young mothers, or underweighting certain emotional and social competencies in assessing leadership suitability – should, as much as possible, be removed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We could also consider a limited number of reservations for female representation on board memberships in GLCs, to preclude the possibility of total non-representation.

sections.label: Childcare and school facilities shortfall
sections.summary: In non-mature estates like Sengkang, childcare and primary school facilities lag the national average as children outnumber facilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a number of non-mature housing estates, especially Sengkang, the constituency that I represent, the ratio of childcare and Primary schooling facilities to eligible-aged children still lags the national average, because even as the absolute number of such facilities has grown, the number of children has grown even faster, resulting in a relative worsening.

sections.label: Board seats and gender pay gaps
sections.summary: The one-fifth board seat target was missed, and the Workers' Party urges gender wage gap reporting and pay gap disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notably, however, the target of at least a fifth of board seats in the top-100 primary-listed companies was missed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While corporate governance matters are, ultimately, incumbent on the leadership of firms themselves, the Workers' Party has emphasised in its manifesto that employers with 10 or more employees should report their gender wage gaps, for the same job, to the MOM.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Remuneration disclosure guidelines for SGX-listed firms should also be revised to encourage the routine publication of the gender pay gap in their annual reports.

sections.label: PAP Women's Wing recommendations
sections.summary: The PAP Women's Wing and Young PAP consulted diverse groups and produced recommendations for the Government to consider.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The PAP Women's Wing and Young PAP have consulted diverse groups in our society, including men, and put together a set of recommendations that we hope the Government will consider to help our women and daughters achieve their fullest potential and aspirations.

sections.label: Sharing parental leave and caregiving
sections.summary: A PAP Women's Wing proposal seeks equal caregiving sharing through parental leave, requiring employer cooperation to encourage men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the proposals in the paper by the PAP Women’s Wing is about ensuring equal sharing of caregiving responsibilities between men and women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is done by sharing of parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The pandemic situation and working from home have made society become more aware about how we can balance caregiving commitments with our jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We also need employers’ cooperation to encourage men to use their parental leave and help to take care of their children at home.

sections.label: Tax reliefs and childcare subsidies
sections.summary: It proposes raising spouse tax relief, extending relief to CPF transfers, and tiered or interim childcare subsidies for non-working mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, the spouse tax relief is lower than an active NSman relief, Parent relief, or the Grandparent Caregiver Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, encourage working spouses to utilise the Retirement Sum Topping-Up Scheme to top up their non-working spouses' CPF accounts by extending tax reliefs to not only cash top-ups, but also CPF fund transfers as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And, perhaps, to introduce a tiered basic childcare subsidy for non-working mothers, in increasing amounts in accordance with the number of children that they have, instead of a flat rate right now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For mothers who are still looking for a job or training for one, perhaps we can have an interim childcare subsidy for a fixed period of time for them.

sections.label: Marriage and Parenthood scheme enhancements
sections.summary: Concerns and survey results were raised to MOH, and in late August 2019 Josephine Teo and Amy Khor announced enhancements to the Marriage and Parenthood scheme, including removing the ART age ceiling and cap, and adding IUI subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: We raised the concerns and survey results to MOH.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: And in late August 2019, Minister Josephine Teo and Senior Minister of State Dr Amy Khor announced enhancements to the Marriage and Parenthood scheme by removing the age ceiling to Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) and also, the cap on the number of times a woman can undergo ART.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: They also added subsidy for couples undergoing Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) at public assistant reproduction centres.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I think there is also no need for another national fertility centre, as we already have three public fertility centres in KKH, SGH and NUH.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: In fact, since mid-2019, couples can proceed with fertility treatments the following month, after completing their consultation and counselling.

sections.label: Women in technology workforce
sections.summary: Women now make up 41% of the technology workforce in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Women now make up 41% of the technology workforce in Singapore.

sections.label: Initiative reach through mentorship
sections.summary: Through mentorship, leadership development, sponsorship and networking opportunities, the initiative has reached out to more than 117,000 people.

sections.label: Jamus Lim on gender equality
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim said gender equality can drive economic progress, noting falling female labour force participation and a substantial gender pay gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim shared how gender equality and female empowerment can be a force for economic progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: He has raised how our female labour force participation rate has actually trended down over the past five years and the male participation rate has consistently outstripped that of women.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: To make matters worse, the gender pay gap in Singapore remains substantial.

sections.label: Manifesto proposals for change
sections.summary: The 2020 manifesto proposals aim to make a difference for women and society by enacting legislative and policy change against discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: This is why we have brought up the various different proposals that we have in our 2020 manifesto and to make a difference, not only for women, but society as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: We have to enact real change in our legislation and Government policies to address discrimination directly.

sections.label: Facets of gender equality
sections.summary: Gender equality involves breaking stereotypes, flexible work, sex education, anti-discrimination laws and fair treatment, and is a national issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Of course, there are many facets to gender equality.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: These include adjusting policies to break down stereotypes which are unfair to women, and allow women to gain more leadership positions, such as in Parliament, the Cabinet and Boards of Directors; introducing measures to encourage employers to adopt flexible work arrangements, to narrow the pay gap between men and women, respect and understand employees’ needs to take care of their family and children; expanding sex education so that people are more sensitive in identifying and preventing sexual harassment and abuse, and giving more protection to children and the less privileged who are vulnerable to sexual harassment and abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: In terms of legislation, the Government can introduce anti-discrimination laws, raise citizens' awareness of gender equality in the workplace and other areas, and strive towards gender equality and fair treatment.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Gender equality and anti-discrimination is not only a women issue, but also a national issue that concerns all of us.

sections.label: Call for parliamentary action
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Parliamentary colleagues will address these issues together, saying it is time for Singapore to take the next step.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: I hope our Parliamentary colleagues will address these issues together, especially since our hon colleagues have, by their own admission, said they raised similar issues repeatedly.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: It is time for Singapore to take the next step.
